summary: A short 1969 note on sending several control messages at once. When a link is blocked, control messages to a host can pile up, and once it is free they should go in one communication; the receiver loops through the messages one by one.

plainLanguage.summary: This very short 1969 note makes one point: when a control line is busy and small messages pile up waiting, it is quicker to send them all in one envelope than to send each one on its own, and the receiver should unpack them one by one.

subtitle: Send multiple control messages together instead of one at a time.

tldr.problem: When a control link is blocked awaiting confirmation, control messages queue up. Sending them one at a time wastes network capacity.
tldr.mechanism: Accumulate control messages while the link is blocked, and send them all together in a single communication when the link becomes available. The receiver loops to decode and process each message.
tldr.outcome: This efficiency principle became standard in protocol design.

today: The unit metadata records the status of RFC 23 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It documents an early best practice for control message batching that influenced later protocol designs.

sections.title: The Problem
sections.content: Network software must handle multiple control messages in a single communication. When the control link is blocked awaiting RFNM (Ready For Next Message), several control messages to a particular remote host may accumulate. Sending them individually would waste efficiency.
sections.plainLanguage: Sometimes the network cannot send right away, so messages pile up. It is better to send them all together.

sections.title: Sending Accumulated Messages
sections.content: When the control link is unblocked (when the RFNM is received), all accumulated control messages should be sent in a single communication for greatest efficiency. Instead of sending each control message in its own packet, batch them together. This approach minimizes the number of control packets transmitted and makes better use of the network bandwidth.
sections.plainLanguage: When the line is ready, send all the waiting messages at once instead of sending each one separately.

sections.title: Receiving Multiple Messages
sections.content: The receiving side must be prepared to handle multiple control messages in a single communication. The receiver needs a loop that decodes and processes successive control messages one at a time, taking appropriate action on each, until the control communication is exhausted. Each control message is independent; processing them in sequence maintains the correct order of operations.
sections.plainLanguage: The receiver reads the control messages one by one from the packet until there are no more.
